prepared_metadata.headline: A free-chain counterexample to a Nash-intersection conjecture
prepared_metadata.name: A free-chain counterexample to a Nash-intersection conjecture
prepared_metadata.description: Complete free-chain Nash intersections give five-blowup counterexamples to a specified reference-divisor assertion, with explicit contact and indexing limits.
prepared_metadata.abstract: We compute the intersection of the closed Nash sets of the complete family of prime divisors obtained by n successive free point blowups over (ℂ²,0), after fixing a prefix of k centers, where 2≤k<n. In suitable coordinates the intersection is {ord x≥⌈n/k⌉, ord y≥n}. For five blowups, fixing two or three centers gives the thresholds (3,5) or (2,5). Neither is q(1,j) for positive integers q,j. These examples disprove the specified-reference-multiple assertion in Conjecture 1 of Fernández de Bobadilla, Pe Pereira and Popescu-Pampu, under each contact and indexing convention explicitly treated here. The source's bare equivalence symbol is undefined and its indexing is inconsistent; no unique author-intended correction is asserted. The intersections are themselves maximal divisorial sets for other toric divisors. Thus the result does not disprove an assertion allowing an arbitrary divisor, or solve the generalized Nash problem.
